## 1. Load and clean the data

Read only the two fund files. Keep the 2018 return and the columns
needed for the nine predictors. Blank entries are treated as missing
(`NA`).

```{r clean-data}
# Read in the datasets
etfs <- read.csv("data/ETFs.csv", na.strings = c("", "NA"))
mutualfunds <- read.csv("data/MutualFunds.csv", na.strings = c("", "NA"))

# Columns to keep
columns <- c(
  "fund_return_2018",
  "fund_annual_report_net_expense_ratio",
  "total_net_assets",
  "inception_date",
  "asset_stocks",
  "asset_bonds",
  "annual_holdings_turnover",
  "fund_price_earning_ratio",
  "fund_sector_technology"
)

# Filter the columns but keep all rows
etfs <- etfs[, columns]
mutualfunds <- mutualfunds[, columns]

# Create indicator variable for etf and mutual fund
etfs$etf_indicator <- 1
mutualfunds$etf_indicator <- 0
funds <- rbind(etfs, mutualfunds)

# Calculate age in years at January 1, 2018
# SERIOUS: FIX THIS YEAR CALCULATION MAY NOT BE CORRECT.
funds$inception_date <- as.Date(funds$inception_date)
funds$fund_age_years <- as.numeric(
  as.Date("2019-01-01") - funds$inception_date
) / 365.25

# Funds launched after that date have no applicable age for this analysis.
funds$fund_age_years[funds$fund_age_years < 0] <- NA

# The model uses age, so the original date column is no longer needed.
# WHY NOT JUST REMOVE THE COLUMN ENTIRELY
funds$inception_date <- NULL

# Check missing values before excluding incomplete rows.
colSums(is.na(funds))

# Keep a separate cleaned table with every model value available.
model_data <- funds[complete.cases(funds), ]

# Compare counts before and after cleaning: 0 = mutual fund, 1 = ETF.
table(funds$etf_indicator)
table(model_data$etf_indicator)
```

Missing stock or bond weights are **unknown, not zero**. A row missing
any required value is excluded from `model_data`, but remains in
`funds`. Recorded zeros and other nonmissing values are kept. No
outliers are removed and no values are filled in. The indicator and age
are the only derived predictors; assets, P/E, weights, expenses,
turnover and returns are unchanged.

## 2. Fit the model

```{r regression}
model <- lm(fund_return_2018 ~ etf_indicator +
    fund_annual_report_net_expense_ratio +
    total_net_assets + fund_age_years +
    asset_stocks + asset_bonds +
    annual_holdings_turnover + fund_price_earning_ratio +
    fund_sector_technology,
  data = model_data
)
```

```{r}

summary(model)
confint(model)  # 95% confidence intervals

```

The ETF coefficient compares ETFs with mutual funds while holding the
other predictors fixed. No transformations or corrections are applied to
this model.

## 3. Summary tables and tests

```{r tables}
summary(model_data)

# Overall test: are all nine predictor coefficients zero?
intercept_only <- lm(fund_return_2018 ~ 1, data = model_data)
anova(intercept_only, model)
```


```{r}

# Test each predictor while accounting for all the others.
drop1(model, test = "F")

# The first column is the response; exclude it from predictor covariance.
covariance_matrix <- cov(model_data[, -1])
knitr::kable(signif(covariance_matrix, 4))
```

The covariance diagonal runs from top left to bottom right and contains
variances. Covariances depend on units, so their sizes alone do not
measure collinearity. Four significant digits are used only to display
the table.

## 4. Graphs

These plots use the original returns and ordinary residuals. A residual
is observed return minus fitted return; calculating it does not
transform the model.

**Boxplot:** compare returns between ETFs and mutual funds.

```{r return-boxplot}
boxplot(fund_return_2018 ~ etf_indicator, data = model_data,
        names = c("Mutual fund", "ETF"),
        ylab = "2018 return (decimal)", main = "2018 returns by fund type")
```

**Histogram:** examine the distribution of returns.

```{r return-histogram}
hist(model_data$fund_return_2018,
     xlab = "2018 return (decimal)", main = "Distribution of 2018 returns")
```

**Residual plot:** look for scatter around zero with no curve or funnel
shape.

```{r residual-plot}
plot(fitted(model), residuals(model),
     xlab = "Fitted return", ylab = "Residual", main = "Residuals versus fitted")
abline(h = 0, col = "red")
```

**Residual vs response per perdictor** 

```{r predictor-residuals, fig.width=10, fig.height=18}
predictor_data <- model$model[, -1]

# Five rows and two columns provide space for nine plots.
par(mfrow = c(5, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

for (predictor in names(predictor_data)) {
  plot(
    predictor_data[[predictor]],
    residuals(model),
    xlab = predictor,
    ylab = "Residual",
    pch = 20,
    cex.lab = 0.8
  )
  abline(h = 0, col = "red")
}

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

**Residuals for predictor:** In this format

```{r residual-pairs, fig.width=16, fig.height=16}
# Get the predictors used in the model.
plot_data <- model$model[, -1]

# Add the residuals as the last column.
plot_data$Residuals <- residuals(model)

# Short labels make the plots easier to read.
names(plot_data) <- c(
  "ETF", "Expense", "Assets", "Age", "Stocks",
  "Bonds", "Turnover", "P/E", "Technology", "Residuals"
)

pairs(
  plot_data,
  pch = 1,
  cex = 0.3,
  col = adjustcolor("black", alpha.f = 0.3),
  main = "Predictors and residuals",

  panel = function(x, y, ...) {
    points(x, y, ...)

    # Residuals on the vertical axis: horizontal zero line.
    if (par("mfg")[1] == ncol(plot_data)) {
      abline(h = 0, col = "red", lwd = 2)
    }

    # Residuals on the horizontal axis: vertical zero line.
    if (par("mfg")[2] == ncol(plot_data)) {
      abline(v = 0, col = "red", lwd = 2)
    }
  }
)
```

**Normal Q-Q plot:** points close to the line support approximately
normal errors; departures at the ends suggest unusual tails.

```{r qq-plot}
qqnorm(residuals(model), main = "Normal Q-Q plot of residuals")
qqline(residuals(model), col = "red")
```

**Residual boxplot:** compare the spread of errors between fund types.

```{r residual-boxplot}
boxplot(residuals(model) ~ model_data$etf_indicator,
        names = c("Mutual fund", "ETF"),
        ylab = "Residual", main = "Residuals by fund type")
abline(h = 0, col = "red")
```

## Notes for later

Excluding missing values can change which funds are represented. Also,
the files contain 2021 reporting dates, so predictor measurements are
not confirmed as pre-2018.
